angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 266,453 km at 35.87 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 27.8783 +/- 0.0217 mas (same row, RUWE 1.19): 35.87 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.383 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Barkaoui et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5720 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract): 266,453 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.383 +/- 0.019 solar masses from Barkaoui et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5720 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3325 +/- 75 K from Barkaoui et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5720 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barkaoui et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5720 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5720.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.855, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
